---
title: "Accounts dataset (WIDE, 2014–2026)"
---

## Summary

This is an open, analysis-ready version of twelve years of UK company accounts, built from
Companies House's free monthly bulk archives. The published table is **WIDE**: one row per company
per accounting period, with the core balance-sheet figures as columns — the table most people want
for modelling. Coverage is continuous from January 2014 to August 2026 (152 monthly archives, no
gaps), and WIDE contains **financial facts and company numbers only** — no names, addresses or
other personal data. The complete as-filed archive (which *does* contain director names, addresses
and loans) is kept private and **never published**.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**The per-fact LONG table has been withdrawn from Kaggle** pending a dimension-aware privacy filter.
A LONG table was briefly published, then deleted when a review found its filter screened concept
names but not dimensional contexts. Only **WIDE** is currently published, and WIDE is unaffected —
its values come only from non-dimensional totals and four reviewed members (see *The WIDE table*
below). LONG will return once the filter screens dimensional contexts too.
:::

The one decision you must make before using WIDE is **which pivot** to read:
`as_first_reported` (what was known at the time — use this for anything predictive) or `latest`
(includes later restatements — do not use it for prediction). Everything else on this page is
about using the tables correctly: the columns, the known limitations, and the licence.

## Details

### The WIDE table

| Table | Grain | Contents | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **WIDE** | one row per (company, period-end) | nine core balance-sheet concepts + equity and creditors splits + helper columns (~2.6 GB Parquet) | **published** |
| **LONG** | one row per fact | a fuller per-fact table across the full concept set | **withdrawn** pending a dimension-aware filter; not currently downloadable |

WIDE is built from genuine non-dimensional totals plus four reviewed dimensional members (the equity
and creditors splits). It **never** includes related-party, officer, director or key-management
contexts — the pivot only admits a dimensionless total or one of those four reviewed
(concept, dimension, member) members, so a dimensional note fact has no WIDE column to land in. The
withdrawn LONG held one row per fact; it returns when its filter screens dimensional contexts, not
only concept names.

Coverage: **152 monthly archives, continuous 2014-01 → 2026-08, 0 gaps.** WIDE has **33,513,017**
rows in `as_first_reported` mode and **36,710,673** in `latest` mode. Source:
`docs/accounts-wide-rebuild-verification.md`, `docs/accounts-limitations.md`. **[Checked]**
(project measurement).

> **Why it starts in 2014, not 2008.** The format WIDE reads (iXBRL) was adopted gradually —
> ~0% of filings in 2010, ~97% by 2014 — so 2014 is where tagged coverage becomes near-universal,
> not where Companies House's data stops. Pre-2014 would be a separate, much lower-fill-rate
> extraction. **Coverage gaps within the span are non-random** — they correlate with filing
> regime, exemption status and company size, so do not treat non-appearance as a random
> exclusion. Source: `docs/accounts-limitations.md`.

### The WIDE columns

The nine core concepts, the dimensional splits, and the helper columns, with coverage measured
on the flagship `as_first_reported` file (33,513,017 rows):

| Column | Meaning | Unit | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `company` | Companies House number (leading zeros preserved) | string | 100% |
| `period_end` | Accounting period end date | date | 100% |
| `Equity` | Total equity (shareholders' funds) | GBP | 75.68% |
| `NetCurrentAssetsLiabilities` | Net current assets/liabilities | GBP | 85.08% |
| `CurrentAssets` | Total current assets | GBP | 78.95% |
| `Creditors` | Total creditors (all maturities) — **sparse; use the splits** | GBP | 3.82% |
| `CashBankOnHand` | Cash and bank balances | GBP | 35.41% |
| `Debtors` | Total debtors | GBP | 35.31% |
| `PropertyPlantEquipment` | Property, plant & equipment (NBV) | GBP | 22.48% |
| `TotalAssetsLessCurrentLiabilities` | Total assets less current liabilities | GBP | 80.63% |
| `AverageNumberEmployeesDuringPeriod` | Average employees during the period | headcount | 60.69% |
| `equity_share_capital` / `equity_retained_earnings` | Equity split | GBP | 30.80% / 29.42% |
| `creditors_within_one_year` / `creditors_after_one_year` | Creditors by maturity | GBP | 32.69% / 13.72% |
| `employees_unit_anomaly` | Was the employee value GBP-tagged? (diagnostic) | 0/1 | 60.69% |
| `n_concepts_present` / `n_source_filings` | Completeness helpers | count | 100% |
| `row_available_yyyymm` | Month by which the whole row was known | YYYYMM | 100% |

The coverage percentages come from the dataset's own **`column-dictionary.md`**, which the
pipeline generates and ships *with* the Kaggle dataset — it is **not** tracked in the git repo
(the `kaggle*/` staging directories are gitignored), so it travels with the download rather than
the source tree. Column *meanings* are also recorded in the tracked
[`docs/accounts-wide-columns.md`](https://github.com/ThomasHSimm/open-company-uk/blob/main/docs/accounts-wide-columns.md).
A matching `accounts-wide-provenance-{mode}.parquet` records which source filing each cell came
from. **[Checked]** (pipeline-generated).

> **Most rows are sparse, and that is expected.** A company reporting only `Equity` and
> `CurrentAssets` for a year genuinely filed filleted accounts without the rest — it is not a gap
> in the extraction. See [the accounts guide](../guide/accounts-data.qmd).

### `as_first_reported` vs `latest`

Both files share the same schema; they differ only in which filing wins each cell.

- **`accounts-wide-as_first_reported.parquet` (flagship, default).** Each cell holds the value
  from the **earliest** filing that reported it — only information available at the time, no
  look-ahead. **Use this for any predictive or point-in-time work.**
- **`accounts-wide-latest.parquet` (secondary).** Each cell holds the value from the **most
  recent** filing, which can include later comparative restatements of an earlier period. **Do
  not use this for predictive work** — a value can reflect information that postdates the period.

Across the full span, **9.36%** of repeated (company, period, concept) values disagree between
first-reported and a later filing, which is exactly why the two files are kept separate rather
than collapsed into one ambiguous "current" column. Source: `docs/accounts-validation-summary.md`,
`docs/accounts-restatement-2014-2026.md`.

### Quickstart

The files are Parquet, so polars, pandas, DuckDB or Spark all work. `row_available_yyyymm` is the
month by which every value in a row had been filed, which makes point-in-time filtering a single
comparison. The company number below (`00012345`) is a placeholder — substitute a real one.

```python
import polars as pl

wide = pl.read_parquet("accounts-wide-as_first_reported.parquet")

# one company's history (company numbers are TEXT — keep the leading zeros)
(wide
   .filter(pl.col("company") == "00012345")
   .sort("period_end"))

# only what was known as of a date: no look-ahead
wide.filter(pl.col("row_available_yyyymm") <= 202312)
```

Rules of thumb, each because it changes how the data should be used:

1. **Pivot mode** — `as_first_reported` for prediction; `latest` leaks the future (~9% of
   repeated figures differ).
2. **Creditors** — use `creditors_within_one_year` / `creditors_after_one_year`; the bare total
   is ~4% populated and unreliable even when present.
3. **Employees** — ~29% are GBP-tagged (median value 1.0, mostly real headcounts). The flag
   marks them; no value is removed. Don't filter employees by unit.
4. **Dashes** — a dash in the accounts means nil and is stored as `0`, not null.
5. **Missing is not zero** — values are never imputed, and some missingness is non-random, so
   decide explicitly how to handle gaps.

Source: deck slides 15–16 and notes (`docs/source-material/companies-house-accounts-deck.md`);
see also [pitfalls](../guide/pitfalls.qmd).

### Limitations to know before modelling

- **Balance-sheet only** for most companies (filleted filing): no turnover or profit.
- **Starts in 2014** — earlier bulk data is barely machine-tagged.
- **Some breakdowns skipped** — facts in multi-member or custom (typed-member) dimensional
  contexts are not captured; ~38% of filings contain at least one such context (these are mostly
  detailed notes, not the balance-sheet totals WIDE uses).
- **Nine core concepts validated** — the other ~4,580 concepts (held in the internal,
  not-currently-published LONG) are captured as filed but **not** validated.
- **Restatements (~9%)** and an **employee reporting break around 2020–2021**.
- **Non-random gaps** — e.g. equity fill-rate varies by more than 10 percentage points across
  months.
- **GBP only in WIDE** — non-sterling filers are excluded (kept in the internal LONG), not converted.

Full detail and every reconciliation: `docs/accounts-limitations.md`. Source: deck slide 17.

### Licence and personal-data policy

Contains public sector information from Companies House, licensed under the **Open Government
Licence v3.0**, free to reuse with attribution. Companies House and the UK Government do not
endorse this dataset, and a derived dataset is not a complete or official representation of any
company.

The published **WIDE** table is **financial facts and company numbers only** — no names, addresses
or director figures (guaranteed by the pivot, which admits only non-dimensional totals and four
reviewed members). The per-fact **LONG** table is **withdrawn from Kaggle** pending a
dimension-aware filter and is not currently downloadable; the private, unfiltered archive that
includes personal data is **never published**. The OGL does not cover personal data.
Source: `docs/accounts-public-long-concepts.md`, `docs/accounts-limitations.md`.
